The bank tops on both sides of the river and the far bank are at street level (ground, H 0); the banks' shore lines stand on the water (support_by).

The bridge deck's heights are the bridge agent's: H = (v of the east face's ground line straight below - v of deck_e)/77, the ground line through the feet se (18810, 1090, est) and ne (20025, 396); the south foot is est (the edge is visible to (18815, 1072)), the north foot firm.

trees.what: A dark, mottled, lumpy mass about 65 px across on the north bank between the handcart's wheel and the bridge's north end post, with an irregular top: a low shrub, or a heap of goods under a cover.
Bare tree with long thin straight twigs fanning upward from a short hidden trunk, beside the western one; no leaves. Medium size.

Willow-like crown of many long thin whips, bare or just leafing, fanning up and out to the west from a trunk hidden behind the crowd at the deck's far (upstream) edge; the western of two such crowns side by side.

Upright pollarded willow just north-east of the leaning one, a straight slender trunk with a knobby head at about (17170-17215, 55-75) and a fan of long bare whips spreading east over the far-bank eating place to about u 17310 and off the silk's top edge.

Old pollarded willow with a thick trunk leaning north-west from the bank top, its knobby head at about (17130, 45-90) sprouting a wide fan of long, thin, bare whips that curve over the far-bank booth and the walled building to the west and run off the silk's top edge. Early spring: no leaves.
Low clump of long pointed leaves or stiff stems (like a clump of tall grass or young bamboo) at the foot of the walled building east of the far-bank shop.

Second willow on the far bank, east of the first: a trunk seen at u 16655-16668 (v 160-235) leaning west near its top to a pollard head at about (16612, 128), its leafless whips fanning up and out between the first willow and the shop to the east.

Willow on the far bank behind the long moored boat: a trunk leaning west from the bank to a knobby pollard head at about (16485, 126), from which long, thin, leafless whips fan out in every direction up to the top of the silk.

Large bare tree between the riverside hall's east gallery and 十千脚店's roof: a straight trunk dividing at a dark knot into many long, thin, upright twigs, with long fine strands hanging down in front of the tavern's west roof.

Large bare tree with stiff, crooked, forking branches (elm-like, no leaves) standing behind the riverside hall's east gable; its trunk leans east toward its foot and its crown spreads west over the water and the hall roof.
A few thin straight stems (shoots, a sapling or a small thicket, no trunk shown) rising from the silk's bottom edge just east of the bare tree's foot.

Bare tree at the silk's bottom edge in front of the hall's east end: two leaders spring from one foot at the bottom edge and fork into stiff, spreading twigs. Its east branch reaches over the edge of 十千脚店's roof.
A second low fan of long bare shoots rising from below the silk's bottom edge in front of the lower building, east of the first: the top of a small tree or shrub whose trunk is below the silk.
A second crown of long bare shoots fanning up from behind the hall's ridge, east of the first and under the big bare tree's lower branches; trunk unseen. Bare, early spring.
Crown of long, straight, bare shoots fanning up from behind the hall's ridge, like the head of a pollarded willow, on the bank between the hall and the river; trunk unseen. Bare, early spring.

A low fan of long, straight, bare shoots rising from below the silk's bottom edge in front of the lower building under the hall, their tips under that building's eave: the top of a small tree or shrub (a pollarded willow's switches?) whose trunk is below the silk.
A bare tree whose short trunk rises from the silk's bottom edge and splits into two stems in a V, with fine upward twigs spreading east and west below the hall's balcony. Unleafed.

A medium bare tree whose leaning trunk enters the silk's bottom edge and forks into a broad crown of fine, straight upward twigs spreading in front of the lower roofs and up to the hall's balcony. Unleafed.

A small bare bush or young tree whose short, forked shoots rise just above the west end of the hall's ridge, on the bank between the hall and the river, east of the old leaning willow's trunk; trunk unseen. Unleafed.

Long, fine, curving whips fanning down and east from a point at the silk's very top edge (about (15495, 20-30)) to about u 15570, v 70: the lower part of a far-bank willow's crown whose head and trunk lie beyond the silk's top edge. Bare, early spring. No hull, cabin or shore line goes with these strokes.

S3.veh.handcart_19862.name: two-wheeled handcart pulled up the north bank
S3.veh.handcart_19862.what: Two-wheeled handcart on the north bank just north of the bridge's north ramp: a slatted box body with two long top rails that run on as shafts at its west end, one big spoked wheel showing on the near side under the body's east half. One man pulls it west by the shafts, a second leans on it at the wheel; no animal is harnessed. No load is drawn above the rails (the box may hold goods).

S3.veh.boat_moored_south_bank_19745.name: boat moored along the south bank
S3.veh.boat_moored_south_bank_19745.what: A long boat moored along the south bank east of the arch, behind (north of) the shops' tiled roofs, which hide its hull below the gunwale: a low dark arched mat roof over its west part (u 19745-20000, v 1080-1150) with three round coils (coiled ropes or round lids) lying on it, a small cabin door at its east end (19958-19991, v 1137-1164), a hatch with an arched frame in the middle (u 20090-20190, v 1070-1110) where two men look out, a long low planked roof over its east part (u 20190-20630, v 1085-1100) with a small arched door or window on its south side at (20345, 1168), and its east end at about u 20630. Two men stand and lie on the roof waving and shouting to the big boat (上下呼救). The dark-trunk tree (t9's) crosses in front of it at u 20380-20460. No mast, sweep or crew working it.

S3.veh.boat_mast_lowering_19518.name: big boat lowering its mast (大船抢险)
S3.veh.boat_mast_lowering_19518.what: The big cargo boat at the bridge, lying crosswise with its squared bow to the west-south-west and its high stern against the north bank: an open forward deck with a windlass and rope drum at the bow (u 19550-19610, v 700-735) and a long striated bundle (the lowered mat sail or coiled cables) over the forward deck (u 19630-19790, v 575-615); a low mat-roofed deckhouse amidships (u 19920-20060, v 575-640) with men under it; a planked after cabin with an open door on its south side (u 20050-20330, v 450-650); a high stern deck (u 20150-20400, v 300-395) and a high stern with its rudder (blade in the water at u 20400-20470, v 560-600). Its A-frame mast is being lowered aft: the legs lie diagonally from the foot amidships (hidden) to the head at (20295, 175), lashed with bindings near the top, with its lines hanging in loose curves down onto the after deck, where the stern crew haul them. Four or five long poles slant from the near-side crew into the water off the south side (lower ends at u ~19730-19990, v 790-810); two crewmen push poles up toward the arch and the cabin boat under it; a long pole held by the man in the cabin door reaches east past the stern to about (20600, 548). A rope thrown from the bridge's crown railing by S3.fig.deck_youth_rope_19445 (t8; the line leaves his hands at about (19471, 244)) hangs in a loop down to about (19600, 420) in front of the cabin boat's roof, toward the forward crew's raised hands; S3.fig.deck_pole_holder_19625 (t8) holds a long pole or taut rope level over the railing at the crown (19585-19658, v 209-228), its far end not painted; S3.prop.bundle_over_rail_19392 (t8) hangs over the railing, perhaps on a rope. Two U-shaped loops hang under the arch's rib at (19772, 392) and (19855, 390): rope loops round the rib or the bridge's iron hooks (conf low). Not rafted; under way, poled.

S3.veh.boat_skiff_19255.name: narrow empty skiff under the arch's south foot
S3.veh.boat_skiff_19255.what: A long, narrow, empty skiff lying in the water under the south half of the arch, parallel to the south bank: a slim hull seen side-on, about 340 px long, its sharp west end running in behind the arch's south leg and its east end rising to an upturned stem with a small knob on its tip; four short uprights (frames or thwarts) stand between gunwale and bottom over its east half. No crew, oar, pole or mooring line is painted.

S3.veh.boat_cabin_under_arch_19225.name: cabin boat under the arch
S3.veh.boat_cabin_under_arch_19225.what: A long boat lying under the bridge's arch, behind (north of) the big boat: a planked hull side with a row of iron cramps (v 525-580), a cabin with a railed open side (posts at u ~19320, 19370, 19420, 19470, 19515, 19585, 19645, 19700; rail v 480-525) and a top beam at v ~445, under a planked roof that disappears behind the arch's rib. Two men lean on the railing looking out at the big boat. No mast, oars or poles show.

S3.veh.sedan_18842.name: sedan chair (车轿相争)
S3.veh.sedan_18842.support: bridge deck: 300 px west of the near edge
S3.veh.sedan_18842.what: Closed sedan chair (轿) going up the bridge's south ramp: a tall dark box with a rounded roof and a lattice window in its front, slung between two long carrying poles that run north-east up the ramp; a bearer at each end. No passenger shows (the box is closed). It is the sedan of the standoff with the horseman higher up the bridge.

S3.veh.barrow_hooped_load_18100.name: big single-wheeled barrow with a hooped load
S3.veh.barrow_hooped_load_18100.what: Large single-wheeled barrow (串车 type) heading west and a little toward the viewer: one big spoked wheel under the front half, the load a mass of bundled goods under arched hoops (a cover frame); a man pushes it from the handles at the east end, a bearded man stands at its front hauling on a rope tied to the balking black donkey west of it (t4's S3.ani.donkey_18048).

S3.veh.boat_mat_cabin_18005.name: boat with a dark mat cabin, moored at the far bank
S3.veh.boat_mat_cabin_18005.what: A boat with a long dark arched mat cabin (18010-18210, v 245-345), two passengers seated inside in the open side (S3.fig.passenger_seated_18112, S3.fig.passenger_seated_18147), and at the east end a mat hood overhanging to a point (18200-18325, v 250-310) above a long low pointed hull end along the waterline (18170-18320, v 365-380) and a vertical post (18240-18260, v 330-370).

S3.veh.chuanche_17775.name: 串车 heaped with a bound load
S3.veh.chuanche_17775.what: 串车 (a barrow-type cart) standing in the open ground in front of the canopy, its huge domed load bound with ropes: a mass of looping, scribbled strokes under big arched hoops, vertical stakes at its west end and a ribbed woven panel (a rolled mat or a basket) at its north-east; two long poles stick out east from the load's top with loops of rope hanging from them, and two long handles run down west-south-west almost to the ground. Nothing draws it: no animal and no puller is painted at either end; two men work at its west (handle) end (t3's).

S3.veh.boat_lowered_mast_17708.name: boat with a lowered mast, moored at the far bank
S3.veh.boat_lowered_mast_17708.what: A long low boat with heavy dark wales or fenders along its side (17710-18000, v 340-375, divided into log-like sections), a low roof (17710-18000, v 255-290) with round objects on its ridge (17900-17990), a lattice rail and bundles of cargo (or potted shrubs) under it; its mast is lowered: a crossed A-frame crutch at the west end (17720-17770, v 190-280) holds a long spar that runs east-north-east over the roof to ~(18100, 208), with rigging lines.

S3.veh.boat_unloading_17705.name: boat unloading at the south bank
S3.veh.boat_unloading_17705.what: A cargo boat moored along the south bank with its bow west toward the 新酒 pole: a short bow beam with a small hanging box (17650-17700, v 820-850), a multi-pronged grapnel anchor (4-5 hooked prongs) hanging under the bow (17700-17780, v 855-930) and a long pole or sweep running from the bow west-south-west over the water to ~(17480, 885); six men stand and bend on the foredeck (17700-17950, v 800-830) over jars and bundles (a jar at (17728, 770-800)); dark sacks or baskets heaped amidships (17900-17990, v 850-890); the stern half (17950-18250) is covered by an arched mat hood (18095-18200, v 735-800) and flat lattice mat awnings on poles (17960-18330, v 740-880; poles at ~18010 and ~18170).

S3.veh.boat_awning_17442.name: boat with a fore awning and mat cabin, moored at the far bank
S3.veh.boat_awning_17442.what: A moored boat, bow west: a pointed bow under a mat awning on a light frame (17365-17510, v 230-300) with poles or oars lying across the foredeck and projecting west to ~17345 (v 300-340), a crouching boatman under the awning at 17420-17470 (S3.fig.awning_boatman_17435; low, or cargo); a large cabin with a high dark mat roof (17510-17760, v 205-240) with a crossed pole frame at its east end; a man sits inside at a window (S3.fig.passenger_seated_17632); bundles of cargo under the roof (17560-17720, v 240-280); two posts with small box lamps or plaques at the cabin's ends (17553, v 265-345, and 17700, v 275-370).

S3.veh.boat_passenger_long_16398.name: long passenger boat moored at the far bank
S3.veh.boat_passenger_long_16398.what: A very long passenger boat with a continuous cabin: at the west (bow) end a deckhouse with open windows (16400-16510, v 245-340), then a long cabin with lattice windows (16500-17060, roof v 245-300, windows v 310-360) with a raised roof section and skylight on top at 16640-16760, a short slanted pole above the roof at (17060-17080, v 225-265), and at the east end a raised upper deckhouse (17150-17330, v 250-300) over a stern cabin; a plank platform and a slanted post (rudder?) at the stern (17250-17345, v 360-395). Moored along the far bank, bow west.

S3.veh.boat_towed_mast_16228.name: masted boat towed by trackers
S3.veh.boat_towed_mast_16228.what: A heavily laden boat with a tall mast (a ladder-like pole with cross cleats, or a bipod seen edge-on) and many stays fanning from the masthead to both ends; big mat-covered cargo heaped high over the bulging stern half (west); a towline runs from the masthead (16075, 45) east-north-east across the water to the rear tracker on the far-bank path (S3.fig.tracker_16333, t2's, at (16325, 112)). At the bow (east) a projecting beam (16170-16235, v 225-250) and a man poling with a long pole into the water (pole foot ~(16245, 308)).

S3.veh.boat_under_way_15595.name: boat under way, sculled with a stern sweep (摇橹向前?)
S3.veh.boat_under_way_15595.what: A mid-sized river boat with a big arched mat roof over most of its length (15610-15900, v 300-470; the restyle tiles it), a high rounded bow at the west end with a curved beam projecting west (15555-15600, v 275-290) and an A-frame of two poles at the bow; three men stand at the bow (on the raised foredeck) and five work a long sweep (橹) over the low stern at the east end: its loom runs from the crew past a pivot at (15965, 503) to a blade lying in the water at 16070-16135, v 555-570. Cargo under the roof (no figures painted inside). No mast up.
